title.narrative: Sustainable Coastal and Marine Fisheries Project

description.narrative:
The project invests in increasing the climate resilience and sustainability of coastal and marine fisheries in Cambodia, targeting the four coastal provinces of Cambodia - Kampot, Kep, Koh Kong, and Preah Sihanouk to reverse the sharp decline in fisheries, promote sustainable mariculture, and enhance fish landing sites to improve seafood safety. It is expected that about 40% of the nearshore fishery will be regenerated into a more productive and sustainable fishery. It will make significant contributions to enhance adaptation to climate change. The project will also promote private sector development by enabling coastal communities and small businesses to diversify their livelihoods, adopt sustainable practices, and scale up into viable enterprises. It will support women's economic empowerment by scaling up women's engagement in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The project will benefit 25 community fisheries (CFi) organizations and members of 15 community protected areas (CPAs), comprising nearly 20,000 households, and a wider coastal community of about 200,000.
The project is aligned with the following impact: coastal and marine fisheries resources made sustainable and resilient. The project will have the following outcome: coastal and marine fish stocks recovered, and diversified climate-resilient income generated. To achieve this outcome, the project has 3 key outputs. Output 1 will support enhancement of adaptive coastal and marine fisheries, which targets changes in the use and management of priority ecosystems and fisheries to reduce the likelihood of their continued decline and build their resilience to underlying climate change threats. Output 2 will support investments in climate-resilient and gender inclusive coastal infrastructure for fisheries management including nature-based infrastructure solutions for coastal erosion, climate risk reduction, and fishery productivity. Output 3 will support incubation and commercialization of sustainable and inclusive marine businesses.

Fish biomass increased by 30% (2022 baseline: TBD) Progress/Status: There are two types of devices involved: 5,000 Fish Protection Structures (FPS) provided by MCC, and 2,500 Fish Boxes supported by the Department of Fisheries Conservation. Fish Protection Structures (FPS):
• A total deployment of 5,000 FPS under MCC. As of Q4 2025, 936 structures have been deployed, with the next priority locations identified in northern Kampot and Sre Ambel. For Sre Ambel specifically, the use of a second-hand barge has been identified as a cost-effective and practical method for deployment, considering the local conditions.
The deployment activities have significantly contributed to the protection and restoration of marine habitats, deterrence to destructive fishing practices in the critcal habitate area and promoting the return of marine mammals such as dolphins and dugongs, as well as the regrowth of seagrass ecosystems. These ecological improvements are fostering opportunities for agritoutism (nature-based tourism), which in turn supports sustainable and reliable livelihoods for local communities. In addition, the project emphasizes community participation and capacity building, ensuring that local people are actively involved including women and youth, and empowered in both the deployment and conservation efforts with skills.
• Fish Boxes: The Department of Fisheries Conservation is overseeing the deployment of 2,500 fish boxes, and has carried out technical consultations and on-site assessments. As of Q4 2025, through series of public consultations 38 locations within CFis in Kep, Kampot, and Preah Sihanouk province were identified and degitaly demacated as potential area for the block deployment, and are scheduled to finish in Koh Kong probince in Q1 2026. In paralel, the two redesigned fish boxes is ready in Q4 2025 for the testing construction and deployment with communities in Kep, and Kampot in Q1 2026. The Department has also compiled X/Y spatial data of previously installed fish boxes supported by other projects, and is reviewing alternative reef structures—particularly from the Sichting ReefSystems Foundation—for compatibility with local marine substrate data. Data Source: Annual monitoring reports for areas where fish productivity structures are deployed. Actual value:

Output: Adaptive coastal and marine fisheries enhanced Indicator: 3,250 ha of benthic species production modernized (2022 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: MAFREDI and MARDEC are being strengthened to support non-feed mariculture, including preparing water and biotoxin monitoring plans, while MARDEC continues to expand hatchery capacity for blue swimming crab, mud crab, and other marine species. Potential pilot sites for blood cockle and green mussel farming have been identified, and Fisheries Institutional Reforms consulting firm (FiA/CS-05- Analyzing Development Issues Centre (ADIC)) is preparing a business plan for MAFREDI.
The roject team has roled out testing sites for green mussel, blood cockle, and rock oyster in 8 sites (4 in Koh Kong, 1 in Preah Sihanouk, and 2 in Kampot and 1 in Kep). Additionally, through various field observation, the expert has prepared for three-year plan for non-feed mariculture to be fully implemented from 2026 onward. Data Source: FiA quarterly progress reports; service provider quarterly reports Actual value:

Construction of Preah Sihanouk FiA Marine Inspectorate Boat Mooring and Jetty (SCMFP FiA/CW-03/2026-01) awarded on 19 Jan 2026.
In Kep, the landing site has been moved and design modifications are underway which needs to (i) extend its pier possibly by 500 meters to access sufficient depth across all tides, (ii) confirm the number and size of vessels that will use the revised site and then reflect this within the revised design as small trawlers are not expected to move to the new site; and (iii) to be gender-responsive and include space for childcare facilities. The change will require a revised social impact consultation, and confirmation of land ownership.
The Sakkadam landing site at the Kep Crab Market is one of Kep's priority sites, is being redesigned at the request of the provincial governor to align with the new tourism development plans, including the upgraded crab market area. Additional priority sites are identified. Social safeguard documents are required for all sites. On the environmental side all the landing sites need a domestic EIA, while the jetty does not.
